title: Conducting Osteochondral Injury Model in Rabbit Knee: Pearls and Pitfalls
author: Vahabi, Er, et al.

steps.title: Select rabbit age
steps.instruction: Use rabbits that are at least 4 months old for the osteochondral injury model.

steps.title: Prepare anesthesia
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal with an intramuscular ketamine‑xylazine injection (preferred for ~20 min surgery) or inhaled sevoflurane if desired.

steps.title: Shave surgical site
steps.instruction: Trim hair with a hair clipper, then shave the area with a razor blade before moving the animal to the surgical table.

steps.title: Cover foot to prevent contamination
steps.instruction: Place a sterile glove or sterile gauze pad over the foot to minimise bacterial colonisation during the procedure.

steps.title: Incise knee and expose joint
steps.instruction: Make a 3 cm midline incision on the anterior knee, pass through skin and subcutaneous tissue, expose the joint capsule, and perform a median parapatellar arthrotomy while keeping the capsule intact on both sides; keep the knee semi‑flexed and identify the midpoint of the trochlea as the defect site.

steps.title: Create guiding hole and drill defect
steps.instruction: Using a 0.5 mm dental burr, make a central guiding entrance hole in the identified area, then enlarge it sequentially with a 2.7 mm drill, a 3.5 mm drill, and finally a 4.5 mm blunt‑ended drill to produce an osteochondral defect of approximately 3 × 4.5 mm (exceeding the 3 × 3 mm threshold). Mark the desired depth on the final drill to ensure consistent depth.

substeps.instruction: Mark intended damage area with a 0.5 mm burr.
Drill 4.5 mm diameter with blunt tip; mark depth on drill.

steps.title: Clean defect and place scaffold
steps.instruction: Flush the created defect with an injector to remove debris, then insert the layered scaffold (bone layer deeper, cartilage layer superficial) ensuring correct orientation.

steps.title: Level scaffold with cartilage
steps.instruction: Adjust the scaffold so that its surface is flush with the surrounding cartilage level, avoiding protrusion or recession.

steps.title: Close joint capsule and skin
steps.instruction: Suture the joint capsule and subcutaneous layer with monofilament absorbable sutures; close the skin with non‑absorbable monofilament synthetic sutures.

substeps.instruction: Use monofilament absorbable sutures for joint capsule.
Use same absorbable sutures for subcutaneous tissue.
Use non‑absorbable monofilament synthetic sutures for skin.

steps.title: Clean incision and post‑op care
steps.instruction: Irrigate the incision with povidone‑iodine solution, apply no dressing, then transfer the animal to a recovery area protected from hypothermia and hypovolemia.

steps.title: Administer antibiotics and wound care
steps.instruction: Give a single daily dose of amoxicillin‑clavulanate for 3 days; perform daily wound care for 2 weeks using either aerosol tetracycline or povidone‑iodine; monitor for suture gnawing and re‑suture if sutures open after the first 3 days.

substeps.instruction: Administer amoxicillin‑clavulanate once daily for 3 days.
Apply topical aerosol tetracycline or povidone‑iodine daily for 2 weeks.
Monitor sutures for gnawing; re‑suture if opened after day 3.

steps.title: Schedule postoperative follow‑up
steps.instruction: Plan a minimum follow‑up period of 6 months (although many studies use 12 weeks) to assess osteochondral healing.

steps.title: Harvest distal femur sample
steps.instruction: After sacrifice, excise the distal femur as a single piece by cutting 3 cm above the joint line with a rongeur or a micro‑oscillating cutter motor, separating it from surrounding capsule and muscle for downstream analysis.
